questions.enonce_markdown:
Distinguish between the following pairs of terms.

(i) Diploid and Haploid

(ii) Gamete and Zygote. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Diploid and haploid**

| Diploid | Haploid |
|---|---|
| A cell or organism with **two complete sets of chromosomes** (chromosomes in **homologous pairs**), written **2n** | A cell with **one set of chromosomes**, written **n** |
| Found in **body (somatic) cells** | Found in **gametes** (sperm, egg cells, pollen grains) |
| Formed by mitosis and at fertilisation | Formed by **meiosis** |

**(ii) Gamete and zygote**

| Gamete | Zygote |
|---|---|
| A **haploid sex cell** (sperm or ovum, pollen nucleus or egg cell) | The **diploid cell** formed when two gametes fuse at **fertilisation** |
| Carries **half** the chromosome number | Has the **full** chromosome number (2n) |
| Produced by **meiosis** in the sex organs | Divides by mitosis to form the **embryo** |

questions.enonce_markdown:
A poultry farmer crossed pure breed white fowls with pure breed black fowls and all offspring were blue. When two of these blue fowls were crossed; it was observed that out of the 492 F$_2$ fowls produced, 121 were black, 125 were white and 246 were blue.

(i) Using appropriate genetic symbols and diagrams, explain the genetics of the crosses. *(12 marks)*

(ii) What is the expected result of a cross between a blue and black fowl? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Explanation**

The F$_1$ fowls are **blue**, a colour different from both parents, and the F$_2$ gives **black : blue : white = 121 : 246 : 125**, which is very close to **1 : 2 : 1** (expected for 492 fowls: 123 : 246 : 123). So neither allele is completely dominant over the other: this is **incomplete dominance (co-dominance)**. The heterozygous fowl shows a **blend**, blue.

Let **$C^B$** = allele for **black** feathers and **$C^W$** = allele for **white** feathers.

| Phenotype | Genotype |
|---|---|
| Black | $C^B C^B$ |
| White | $C^W C^W$ |
| Blue | $C^B C^W$ |

**First cross (P generation)**

- Parents (phenotypes): black fowl $\times$ white fowl
- Parents (genotypes): $C^B C^B$ $\times$ $C^W C^W$
- Gametes: $C^B$ and $C^W$
- F$_1$ genotype: all $C^B C^W$; F$_1$ phenotype: **all blue**

**Second cross (F$_1 \times$ F$_1$)**

- Parents (genotypes): $C^B C^W$ $\times$ $C^B C^W$ (blue $\times$ blue)
- Gametes: $C^B$ , $C^W$ $\times$ $C^B$ , $C^W$

| Gametes | $C^B$ | $C^W$ |
|---|---|---|
| **$C^B$** | $C^B C^B$ (black) | $C^B C^W$ (blue) |
| **$C^W$** | $C^B C^W$ (blue) | $C^W C^W$ (white) |

- F$_2$ genotypes: 1 $C^B C^B$ : 2 $C^B C^W$ : 1 $C^W C^W$
- F$_2$ phenotypes: **1 black : 2 blue : 1 white**, which agrees with the observed 121 : 246 : 125 (about 25 % : 50 % : 25 %).

**(ii) Cross between a blue and a black fowl**

- Parents: blue $C^B C^W$ $\times$ black $C^B C^B$
- Gametes: $C^B$ , $C^W$ $\times$ $C^B$

| Gametes | $C^B$ |
|---|---|
| **$C^B$** | $C^B C^B$ (black) |
| **$C^W$** | $C^B C^W$ (blue) |

Expected result: **1 black : 1 blue**, that is **50 % black and 50 % blue** fowls (no white fowls).
